newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - 28 July.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - 28 July.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- BACKDATED TAX RISE TO HIT FRENCH COMPANIES

The French government has unveiled plans to levy a higher tax rate for French companies and the French subsidiaries of multinational companies with a rise to a 41.6 per cent tax rate from the present 36.6 per cent to apply for the financial year from January 1 1997. Companies not having a financial year end on 31 December, such as Air France, Moulinex and Salomon, are expected to pay the higher rate tax for the 1996 financial year.
-- VODAFONE PLANS FIXED TELECOMS SERVICES DEAL

Chief executive for the mobile phone group Vodafone, Chris Gent, has announced that the company is soon to make a deal to sell the services of the National Grid-owned telecommunications network Energis to become the first mobile phone operator to offer a fixed telecoms service. The plan includes a comprehensive mobile/fixed phone service offering voice telephony, data communications and private networks.
-- EUROPEAN BANKS TO DRAFT CODE FOR SELLING ON LOANS

Leading European banks are to draw up a code to trade syndicated loans which will require agreement from the borrowers for the loans to be sold off on a US-style secondary market that allows banks to transfer loans to other lenders. The move follows an initiative by more than 100 of the worlds leading banks to create the Loan Market Association last year which advocates the loan plans that are expected to bring increased competition into the syndicated loans business.
-- BIG GROUPS TO FACE STATUTORY INTEREST ON LATE BILLS

In a consultative government green paper issued by the department of trade and industry, businesses have until October 3 to reply to the problem of late bill payment or the government may introduce plans to charge statutory interest on large companies' late payment of bills to smaller firms. The move comes as part of a government initiative to address late payment and counter the disproportionate damage larger companies can have on smaller firms.
-- BUDGET DEFICIT ERROR DEALS BLOW TO FINNS

Due to a unexplained statistical error the Finnish government has had to revise its 1996 budget deficit upwards to 3.1 per cent from 2.6 per cent of gross domestic product. The embarrassing error for Finland and the EU has highlighted the difficulties that are involved in obtaining accurate data for the European Commission to help them decide next spring on which countries can enter the EMU. The Commission earlier this year recommended that Finland should come off the blacklist of counties to qualify for the EMU entry under the Maastricht ruling of 3 per cent of GDP.
-- RISING POUND HITS SMALLER EXPORTERS

A report by the Confederation of British Industry and chartered accountant Pannell Kerr Forster has revealed that small and medium sized businesses have struggled in the export market under the strength of the pound just as much as their larger competitors. The report shows that new exports for smaller companies are falling at their fastest rate in six years offering implications for the Bank of England's decision on interest rate changes for the month of August after three consecutive months of rate increases.

-- HACKNEY AWARDS 70M STG IT CONTRACT Birmingham-based managed services provider ITnet have won a 70m stg contract to run all of the London Borough of Hackney's revenues and benefits services for ten years saving the council an estimated 2.5m stg a year. ITnet, a management buy-out firm from Cadbury Schweppes in 1995, competed with other companies for the much sought after contract that precedes the Treasury's private finance initiative review that is due for release this week.
-- EUROPE SET TO REMAIN OVERBANKED

After the agreed merger of big German banks Bayerische Vereinesbank and Bayerische Hypobank last week investors have speculated about the possible wave of similar mergers across European banks with ABN Amro Hoare Govett launching a cell warrant with a geared bet on shares of 15 banks likely to improve their performance through mergers or internal restructuring that increased 75 per cent in value in the space of a week.
-- HUGO BOSS UP 25 PER CENT IN QUARTER

German men's clothing company Hugo Boss, owned by Italian group Marzotto, announced first-half net income had increased 25 per cent to DM38.5m with turnover up 17 per cent to DM530m boosting preference share prices by 7 per cent to close at DM2,150 against analysts expectations. The company attributes much of its success to organic growth with further contributions derived from the dollar's rise.
-- MICROSOFT SAYS GROUP'S SHARES ARE OVERPRICED

US software company Microsoft has protested that the Wall street valuation of $160bn, that last week put the company as the second most highly valued after General Electric, is overpriced considering the short life cycle of the company's products and volatility of its market. The company's annual meeting with financial analysts last week heard company executives warn of future pitfalls and the rising costs and competitive challenges that the company will have to face.
